description: Field engineer healer - patches one ally and lets the overflow wash across the rest of the party.
_source_note: Rebuilt 5 Nov 2026 from data/reference/coa/tinker.json tab 74 (37 real CoA Invention talents) with identity from data/reference/coa_playstyles.json ('Restoration Shaman + Holy Paladin', Healer). Replaces a 27-node tree that carried real CoA names on fifteen 2-4% scalars and had exactly one proc in it. The twelve unlock_ability nodes were already correct and are kept. Every node below records the CoA text it came from and what was changed for a turn-based engine.

nodes.name: Scientific Nature
nodes.description: Increases your healing power by 12% of your Intellect and your spell critical strike chance by 15% of your Intellect.
nodes._source: CoA verbatim: 'Level 20 Passive. Increases your healing power by 20% of your Intellect and your critical strike rating by 15% of your Intellect.' Built as the real stat conversion it is - both pairings are in STAT_CONVERSION_TARGETS/SOURCES, so both are live. Was healing_power_pct 2.0 per rank over 5 ranks, which is a flat 10% and not this talent at all.

nodes.name: Over-Repaired
nodes.description: Increases the healing done by Repair Shot by 15% per rank.
nodes._source: CoA verbatim: 'Increases the healing done by Repair Shot by 15%.' 2 ranks, as CoA has it.

nodes.name: Field Medic
nodes.description: Increases your spell critical strike chance by 6%.
nodes._source: CoA: 'Increases your and your summons critical strike chance by 5%.' The summon half is dropped: no talent key reaches a pet's crit. crit_chance_spell is a PERCENT here, so 5.0.

nodes.name: Technician
nodes.description: Increases the critical strike damage of your spells by 20% per rank.
nodes._source: Standardised 6 Nov: every caster tree carries one 5-point spell-crit-damage talent worth +100% at full rank, matching priest_shadow's Shadow Power and shaman_elemental's Elemental Fury (both WoW-accurate). Kyle: 'all caster classes should have a 5 point talent that increases their spell crit damage by 100%.'

nodes.name: Build: ZIGGI-6K
nodes.description: Learn Build: ZIGGI-6K. A regenerative drone that heals your allies until dismissed.
nodes._source: CoA: 'Level 10 Passive. Teaches you Build: ZIGGI-6K.' Kept from the previous tree - the unlock nodes were already right.

nodes.name: Healing Radiator
nodes.description: Learn Healing Radiator. Periodic healing from Nanobot Reconstruction leaks out to the rest of the party.
nodes._source: CoA: 'Periodic healing done by Nanobot Reconstruction now restores health to 5 allied players within 10 yds of the affected target.' The yard radius is dropped; the ability itself already targets the party. Kept from the previous tree.

nodes.name: Eureka!
nodes.description: Your critical heals send a surge of healing to your most wounded ally.
nodes._source: CoA: 'Direct healing critical strikes now increase the healing done by your next Repair Shot or Emergency Heal by 30% for 10 seconds.' NOT buildable as written, and this is the one node in the tree where that is worth spelling out. A 'your next cast is stronger' buff has to reach ability_tinker_repair_shot_healing, which is read ONLY through get_talent_effects() - and that aggregates talent trees, stances, forms and the guardian stance, never status effects. A proc applying that buff is dead data. So the 30% is spent where it does fire: smart_heal_pct, which heals the lowest-health ally off the crit that triggered it. Note smart_heal_pct is a PERCENT (status_effects.py divides by 100), unlike every other heal payload here, which are fractions.

nodes.name: Nanobot Swarm
nodes.description: Learn Nanobot Swarm. Nanobots ride an ally, damaging nearby enemies and pulling your threat onto the host.
nodes._source: CoA: 'Send Nanobots to an ally, dealing damage to nearby enemies every 4 sec for 1 min. All threat generated by you is redirected to the target.' Kept from the previous tree.

nodes.name: Triage Protocol
nodes.description: Your healing is 9% stronger on allies below 35% health.
nodes._source: Not a CoA node - kept from the previous tree, where it was 3%, because it is one of the few things in that tree that was a real mechanic rather than a flat number. low_health_healing_pct keys off the RECIPIENT's health and was genuinely dead for a while; it was wired up at abilities.py:1574 once the heal path started passing the recipient through, and audit_talents.py's docstring still says otherwise. Threshold is the engine-wide low_health_threshold_pct default of 35%.

nodes.name: Nanobot Cleanser
nodes.description: Learn Nanobot Cleanser. Nanobots strip a poison and a disease from an ally each turn.
nodes._source: CoA: 'Send Nanobots to an ally removing 1 poison and disease effect every 3 sec for up to 15 sec.' Kept from the previous tree; 3 sec per tick is already one turn.

nodes.name: Nanobot Reconstruction
nodes.description: Learn Nanobot Reconstruction. A sustained repair patch that mends an ally over several turns.
nodes._source: Kept from the previous tree. The ability Healing Radiator spreads, so it has to be learnable before it.

nodes.name: Fine Tuning
nodes.description: Increases your spell critical strike chance by 3%.
nodes._source: CoA: 'Increases critical strike chance of all party and raid members by 3%. Does not stack with similar effects. In addition, not critically healing now increases your critical strike chance by 1%, stacking 10 times, until your next effective critical heal.' Two halves, neither portable as written. A talent effect applies to its own character, so the party-wide aura becomes self-only and the description says 'your' rather than promising the party a buff it will not get. The stacking half needs a 'healed and did NOT crit' trigger, which no trigger in this engine expresses - on_heal_cast cannot see the crit result - so it is dropped rather than approximated.

nodes.name: Macro Designer
nodes.description: Increases the duration of Med Pack by 1 turn.
nodes._source: CoA: 'Increases the duration of your Beacons by 5 sec and Med Pack by 3 sec.' 3 sec is one turn. The Beacon half is dropped: Frontier's Beacons are party buffs whose duration no ability_*_duration key reaches, while Med Pack is a hot and does take one.

nodes.name: Stim Rounds
nodes.description: Learn Stim Rounds. Load stim rounds into your gun, so your shots carry a dose of medicine.
nodes._source: Kept from the previous tree. tinker_stim_rounds carries requires_talent, so this node is the ONLY way the ability can be learned - dropping it would strand the ability at every level. Paired deliberately with Stim Augmentation, which is what makes the dose splash.

nodes.name: Stim Augmentation
nodes.description: Your Repair Shot splashes 20% of its healing onto up to 3 nearby allies.
nodes._source: CoA verbatim: 'Add a Stim Augmentation to your gun for 1 hour, causing your direct healing abilities to heal up to 3 nearby allies for an additional 20% of the amount healed.' This is the spec's defining mechanic and the old tree had no form of it. splash_heal is a live proc payload with a max_targets field, so CoA's number goes in directly. The 1-hour self-buff framing is dropped - a weapon augmentation lasting an hour is a passive in this engine. pct is a FRACTION.

nodes.name: Med Pack
nodes.description: Learn Med Pack. A pack that keeps mending an ally for several turns.
nodes._source: Kept from the previous tree.

nodes.name: Bandage Gun
nodes.description: Your Emergency Heal and Zap! splash 20% of their healing onto up to 5 nearby allies.
nodes._source: CoA verbatim: 'Healing from Stim Augmentation now affects 2 additional allies near the primary target.' A talent cannot widen ANOTHER talent's proc - there is no key that edits a sibling node's max_targets - so instead of faking that, this node carries its own splash at CoA's widened count (3 + 2 = 5) over the other two direct heals. Net effect matches what the pair is for: spending both points means the whole direct-heal kit splashes, and widely. Was a 3% cost reduction.

nodes.name: Stim Shots
nodes.description: Increases the healing done by Repair Shot and Emergency Heal by 6%.
nodes._source: CoA: 'Your Stim Augmentation now heals for an additional 10% of the amount healed.' Routed onto the heals themselves rather than onto the splash: the splash is sized from the triggering heal, so raising the heal raises the splash with it, and there is no key that reaches a proc's own pct.

nodes.name: Zap!
nodes.description: Learn Zap. A long jolt of current that mends an ally. Scales with Repair Shot.
nodes._source: Real screenshot: Requires Level 38, Zap! (Rank 1) - real self-rank gate, Kyle-confirmed. Kept from the previous tree.

nodes.name: Build: Battery Reclaimer
nodes.description: Learn Build: Battery Reclaimer. A station that gives the party back health and resources.
nodes._source: CoA: 'Build a Battery Recharge Station for 30 sec that allies can interact with once to replenish 15% maximum health and mana, and 50% maximum Rage, Energy, Focus and Runic Power. Applies Depleting Battery to party and raid members within 40 yds.' The movement-speed aura and the 'run to the battery' interaction are both positional and both dropped. Kept from the previous tree.

nodes.name: Trust the Science!
nodes.description: Reduces the cooldown of Zap! by 12%.
nodes._source: CoA: 'Reduces the cooldown of Zap! by -5 sec.' Expressed as a percentage because a flat 5 sec is under two turns and would round to nothing useful. NOTE the sign convention: _cooldown_pct is POSITIVE for a reduction here, so 0.20 makes Zap! cheaper to come back to, not slower.

nodes.name: Resourceful Tech
nodes.description: Increases the critical strike chance of Zap! by 21%.
nodes._source: CoA: 'Your Zap! is now guaranteed to critically strike allies affected by Nanobots.' The condition is what balances it, and no effect key can read whether the heal target carries a specific buff. Shipped as a large but not guaranteed crit bonus instead of an unconditional ability_tinker_zap_crit of 100.0, which is what the literal reading would have been and would have been a permanent free crit. ability_*_crit is a PERCENT.

nodes.name: Rejuvenating Gadget
nodes.description: Critical strikes with Zap! leave behind rejuvenating gas, healing the target for 3 turns.
nodes._source: CoA: 'Critical strikes with Zap! now apply Rejuvenating Gas to up to 12 allies within 8 yards of your target that restores 15% of the value of the shot as health every 2 sec for 10 sec.' The 12-ally yard radius is dropped (no positioning) and the hot lands on the heal target. A proc-applied hot has a flat potency - there is no 'percentage of the triggering amount' form for apply_effect - so 15% of a Zap! is approximated as a flat 24 per turn, in the same range as Frontier's other mid-level hots.

nodes.name: My Greatest Invention!
nodes.description: Learn My Greatest Invention. Show off the masterpiece, healing the whole party over several turns.
nodes._source: Kept from the previous tree.

nodes.name: Improved Graftbolts
nodes.description: Your Repair Shot also shields the target for 50% of the healing done.
nodes._source: CoA: 'Level 50 Passive. Effective healing done by Stim Augmentation now applies a shield to the target equal to 50% of the healing done. Up to 10% of their maximum health.' shield_pct is a live payload sized from the triggering heal, which is exactly this. The 10%-max-health cap is NOT modelled: shield_pct has no cap field, and absorb_pct_max_health sizes off max health instead of off the heal, so it is the wrong mechanism. Flagged rather than faked - this node is slightly stronger than CoA's on a very large heal. CoA's base Graftbolts (a pet mana/damage buff off a 25% chance) is not built at all: it hangs entirely on a mechanical pet's own output, which no talent key reaches.

nodes.name: Emergency Circumvented
nodes.description: Increases the critical strike chance of Emergency Heal by 9%.
nodes._source: CoA: 'Increases the critical strike chance of Emergency Heal by 15% and allows the periodic healing done by Med Pack to critically strike.' The second half is an engine-wide rule about whether hot ticks can crit, not a per-character bonus, so it is not a talent effect at all and is dropped.

nodes.name: Self-Sustaining Technology
nodes.description: 15% of the healing you do is also routed to your most wounded ally.
nodes._source: CoA: 'Damage or healing done by your pet or summons now heals you equal to 15% of the value. In addition, damage or healing done by you now restores health and mana to your pet equal to 15% of the value. Each of these effects can only occur once per sec.' Both halves of CoA's version are pet-side and unreachable. The identity worth keeping is 'your output feeds back into the group', so leech_pct with smart:true sends it to the worst-off ally. CoA's once-per-second becomes icd 1, i.e. once a turn. Was max_mana_pct 0.02.

nodes.name: Surge Protector
nodes.description: While above 65% mana, your healing is 3% stronger.
nodes._source: Not a CoA node - kept from the previous tree (where it was 3%) for the same reason as Triage Protocol: it is a real conditional rather than a flat number. high_mana_healing_pct fires above 1 - low_health_threshold_pct of max mana, i.e. 65%, and pairs with Triage Protocol's low-health window.

nodes.name: Emergency Enhancer
nodes.description: Zap! now also fires from your active constructions, healing your most wounded ally for 90% of the amount.
nodes._source: CoA: 'Zap! now causes your active Build abilities to zap the lowest health nearby ally, healing them for 990 + 90% healing.' smart_heal_pct is the payload for 'heal the lowest-health ally' and this is almost a literal port - the only cut is the flat 990, which is a level-60 raid number. PERCENT, so 90 means 90% of the Zap! that triggered it.
